chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

In the case of a man who had a wife under him, then he divorced her, and then he died regarding her before her waiting period ended, he said: She observes the waiting period of the longer of the two periods, the waiting period of the one whose husband died regarding her.

key_terms.أَبْعَدَ الْأَجَلَيْنِ: The longer of the two periods
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: Waiting period (Iddah) for divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a divorced woman if her husband dies before her divorce is finalized?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Istibsar* to resolve the jurisprudential debate regarding the 'iddah of a woman in a revocable divorce (*raj'i*) upon her husband's death. The hadith establishes the principle of *tarajjuh* (preponderance), requiring her to observe the longer of the two waiting periods—death or divorce—to ensure absolute certainty in her marital status before remarrying. This reflects the Shia emphasis on caution in personal status laws to prevent lineage confusion.
